description: We are high school students in Toronto, Ontario, with keen interests in engineering, design, and build. We enjoy building models, and solving complex problems. We joined this challenge to portray our skills in design and coding.
summary: My team and I researched and developed a script on the chronicles of the last days of the NEAR Shoemaker instrument left on Mars. Along with a script, a 3 episode podcast series was made with each episode describing the chronological events of this instrument. It is important as it was the first one to land on an asteroid, helping scientists study how to protect Earth from space hazards.
details:
Our project, The Last Signal, is a three-part podcast series about NASA's NEAR Shoemaker spacecraft and its historic landing on asteroid 433 Eros. Through three episodes, we explore its journey, unexpected landing, final communication with Earth, and the possibility of retrieving the spacecraft.

Benefits and Intended Impact: Our podcast presents space exploration in an interesting and accessible way. It raises awareness about asteroid research and demonstrates how scientific missions can continue to provide value even after they end.


Tools and Software: We used Canva to organize and assemble our podcast episodes, along with narration, background music, and sound effects to create an engaging audio experience.


Creativity: We chose a podcast instead of a conventional presentation, using suspense, storytelling, radio static, beeping sounds, and spacecraft sound effects to recreate the atmosphere of deep-space exploration and keep listeners interested.

Factors Considered: We prioritized scientific accuracy, historical details, audience engagement, episode duration, sound quality, and the practicality, costs, and challenges of potentially retrieving the spacecraft.
